title: Control Plane ACL
description: A default control plane ACL is provided and applied to the system control-plane. The default control-place ACL is read-only, but you can create and assign a different ACL to the system control-plane if customization is needed. However, it is strongly recommended to use the default control-plane ACL as a template for any custom ACL that you may apply to ensure protocol and management operations function correctly. The default control plane ACL filters all IP traffic inbound and outbound on any management interface. SSH, Telnet, NTP, SNMP, IP protocols, and logging/matching on management traffic are done by this ACL. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.2 Control Plane ACL

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Run the following command to check that either your custom ACL or the default ACL is applied switch#show running-config all section system control-plane system control-plane ip access-group custom-control-plane-acl in ip access-group default-control-plane-acl vrf MGMT in switch# The control plane ACL is referenced by the ip[v6] access-group <ACLNAME> in configuration.

remediation.command:
! Apply a control plane ACL to the default vrf and all non default vrfs
system control-plane
ip access-group custom-control-plane-acl in
ip access-group custom-control-plane-acl vrf MGMT in

title: NTP authentication
description: NTP authentication verifies that time updates come from a trusted server, preventing bad actors from spoofing time or altering your clock. The NTP authentication model is the opposite of the typical client-server authentication model. NTP authentication enables an NTP client or peer to authenticate time received from their servers and peers. Authentication support allows the NTP client to verify that servers are in fact known and trusted and not intruders intending accidentally or intentionally to masquerade as a legitimate server. Requires 'ntp authentication-key' and 'ntp trusted-key'. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.5 NTP authentication

remediation.command:
ntp authentication-key 1 sha1 timesync
ntp trusted-key 1

title: Syslog with TLS support
description: Syslog over TLS is a secure standard (RFC 5425) that encrypts log messages in transit using Transport Layer Security. It protects sensitive operational and security data from interception and tampering. Syslog messages may transit several hops to arrive at the intended collector. Some intermediary networks may not be trusted by the originator, relay, or receiver because the network is in a different security domain or at a different security level from the ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.9 Syslog with TLS support

remediation.command:
! 1. Create an SSL profile
ssl profile syslog-profile
certificate clientCert key ClientKey
trust certificate serverCA
2. Define syslog server
logging vrf MGMT host 10.1.1.1 protocol tls ssl-profile syslog-profile

title: Enable AES-GCM Encryption of EOS Secrets
description: AES-GCM has been added as a method for storing symmetric secrets in EOS. This applies to secrets that must be used to remote systems, as found in NTP, TACACS+, and other places. A new secret type "8a", which stands for AES-256-GCM encryption type, has been introduced. Secrets can either be entered in type 0, plaintext, and automatically converted or entered directly as type 8a. The default method of storing shared secrets is to obfuscate them in the running configuration. This obfuscation mean secrets can be easily reversed by copying the configuration out of the box. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Enable AES-GCM Encryption of EOS Secrets

remediation.command:
conf
management security
password encryption reversible aes-256-gcm

title: Do not allow remote login without a password
description: The default switch configuration allows usernames that are not password-protected to log in only from the console. It is possible to configure the switch to allow unprotected usernames to log in from any port. Allowing remote access to accounts without passwords is a severe security risk. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.1 Do not allow remote login without a password

remediation.command: Reset the feature to the default value #default aaa authentication policy local allow-nopassword-remote-login

title: Configure an enable password
description: The enable command controls access to Privileged EXEC and all configuration command modes. The enable password authorizes users to execute the enable command. When the enable password is set, the CLI displays a password prompt when a user attempts to enter Privileged EXEC mode. It is recommended that the enable secret password be used at all times to grant administrative access to the Arista switch. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.2 Configure an enable password

remediation.command:
! Configure and enable password
enable password {password string}

title: Create a password complexity policy
description: A password policy can be used to mandate password requirements. The policy enforces recommendations when creating local users. Requires a password policy with 'minimum length' of at least 8 under 'management security'. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.3 Create a password complexity policy

remediation.command:
! management security
password policy PasswordPolicy
minimum length 8
minimum special 1
minimum upper 1
minimum lower 1
minimum digits 1
exit
management accounts
password policy PasswordPolicy

title: Verify root login is disabled
description: EOS can be configured to allow logging in as root directly by using the aaa root secret config command. This should be not be enabled. An authenticated, authorized user can obtain superuser access after logging in by accessing the bash shell if permitted. Allowing remote root login bypasses the EOS cli and gives direct access to the bash shell. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.4 Verify root login is disabled

remediation.command:
! Reset to default value
default aaa root

title: Configure TACACS+/RADIUS server
description: The switch defines a TACACS+ server connection by its address and port. It is recommended to use two or more authentication servers for the purpose of granting administrative access. At least one TACACS+ server must be configured. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5.1 Configure TACACS+/RADIUS server

remediation.command:
! This command configures the switch to communicate with the TACACS+ server assigned the host name TAC_1 using the encryption key rp31E2v.
tacacs-server host TAC-1 key rp31E2v

title: Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting
description: The use of Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) affords the best methods for controlling user access, authorization levels, and activity logging. By enabling AAA on the switches in conjunction with an authentication server such as TACACS+ or RADIUS the administrators can easily add or remove user accounts, add or remove command authorizations, and maintain a log of user activity. The Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) framework is essential to securing a network device. The AAA framework provides a mechanism to authenticate and limit specific actions being performed within a management session. Requires group-based login authentication, exec authorization and command authorization. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5.3 Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting

audit.pattern: (?m)(?s:^aaa authentication login default group \S.*^aaa authorization exec default group \S.*^aaa authorization commands all default group \S)|(?s:^aaa authentication login default group \S.*^aaa authorization commands all default group \S.*^aaa authorization exec default group \S)|(?s:^aaa authorization exec default group \S.*^aaa authentication login default group \S.*^aaa authorization commands all default group \S)|(?s:^aaa authorization exec default group \S.*^aaa authorization commands all default group \S.*^aaa authentication login default group \S)|(?s:^aaa authorization commands all default group \S.*^aaa authentication login default group \S.*^aaa authorization exec default group \S)|(?s:^aaa authorization commands all default group \S.*^aaa authorization exec default group \S.*^aaa authentication login default group \S)

remediation.command:
! Configure AAA. Servers should be reachable via the management vrf.
aaa group server tacacs+ TACPLUS
server {ip address} vrf {management vrf}
server {ip address2} vrf {management vrf}
exit
aaa authentication default enable group TACACS+ local
aaa authentication login default group TACPLUS local
aaa authentication enable default group TACPLUS local
aaa authorization exec default group TACPLUS local
aaa authorization commands all default group TACPLUS local

title: Limit SSH Access Only To The Network Management Segment
description: The network element should only allow management connections for administrative access from hosts residing in the management network. It is recommended to review the configuration and verify management access to the device is allowed only from hosts within the management network. Requires SSH to be shut down in the default VRF (enable it only under the management VRF). Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.6.1 Limit SSH Access Only To The Network Management Segment

remediation.command:
! management ssh
sho active
vrf MGMT
no shutdown
exit
shutdown
end

title: Set Idle Timeout for SSH to 10 Minutes or Less
description: Idle ssh sessions can be re-used by unathorized users who have access to an unlocked workstation where a network admin has connected to network devices via ssh and has stepped away. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.6.2 Set Idle Timeout for SSH to 10 Minutes or Less

remediation.command: management ssh idle-timeout 10

title: Ensure SNMP Community
description: Only allow SNMP read access and ensure that the default or well-known SNMP community strings public and private are not used. An ACL should be used to further restrict which remote hosts can query the switch. Enabling write access to the device via SNMP provides a mechanism that can be exploited by an attacker to set configuration variables that can disrupt network operations. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.7.2 Ensure SNMP Community

remediation.command: no snmp-server community public no snmp-server community private snmp-server community {community string} ro {snmp security acl}

title: Telnet access
description: Telnet transmits credentials and data in cleartext. It is disabled by default and should not be enabled. Telnet is an obsolete protocol vulnerable to eavesdropping. Telnet is shut down by default (block not shown); fails if 'management telnet' has 'no shutdown'. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.8 Telnet access

remediation.command:
! Disable telnet
conf
management telnet
shutdown
end

title: API access using https
description: The Arista Command eAPI is a simple and complete API that allows you to configure and monitor your Arista switches. Once the API is enabled, the switch accepts HTTPS requests containing a list of industry standard CLI commands, and responds with machine-readable output and errors serialized in JSON (served over HTTP or HTTPS). HTTP can be enabled but should be left disabled. EOS API provides structured output more suitable for programmatic parsing than cli scraping. If the API is enabled, it should only use https, not http. Fails if eAPI has plain 'protocol http' enabled. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.9 API access using https

remediation.command:
! management api http-commands
no shutdown
default protocol http
vrf MGMT
no shutdown

title: OSPF Interface Authentication
description: OSPF authentication secures routing updates by verifying the identity of neighboring routers, preventing malicious devices from injecting false routing information. The OSPFv2 Secure Hash Algorithms (SHA) Authentication support as defined in RFC 5709 supports the configuration of SHA1, SHA256, SHA384 and SHA512 Message-Digest authentication as an alternative to the MD5 Message-Digest authentication. Because a routing protocol contains information that need not be kept secret, privacy is not a requirement. However, authentication of the messages within the protocol is of interest in order to reduce the risk of an adversary compromising the routing system ... Passes when OSPF is not configured. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.1 OSPF Interface Authentication

remediation.command: Configure OSPF authentication on interfaces connected to OSPF neighbors interface {interface-name} ip ospf authentication message-digest ip ospf authentication message-digest-key {number} sha256 {key text}

title: ISIS Interface and Instance Authentication
description: Enable authentication of ISIS hellos on interfaces and LSPs, CSNPs, and PSNPs for the protocol instance. IS-IS authentication secures routing adjacencies and LSDB updates by validating the source of protocol packets. Passes when IS-IS is not configured. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.2 ISIS Interface and Instance Authentication

remediation.command: interface Ethernet {X} isis authentication mode md5 isis authentication key {key} router isis {protocol instance} authentication mode md5 authentication key {key}

title: BGP Authentication
description: The neighbor password command enables authentication on a TCP connection with a BGP peer. When utilizing BGP the threat profile becomes much larger as routes external to the data center will be updating routing information in the devices. Much like with the IGP an attacker could redirect traffic to an insecure location where traffic could be ... Passes when BGP is not configured; otherwise requires a neighbor password. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2.1 BGP Authentication

remediation.command: Configure passwords for each neighbor as appropriate router bgp neighbor {IP address} password

title: BGP TCP Authentication Option (TCP-AO)
description: BGP TCP Authentication Option (TCP-AO) (RFC 5925) support adds a new option for BGP message and TCP segments authentication using superior hashing algorithms such as HMACs and CMACs as an improvement over TCP MD5, with stronger hashing algorithms providing higher security and protection against replays attacks. EOS supports BGP message authentication via the TCP MD5 Signature (TCP MD5) option (RFC 2385) to protect the BGP sessions from spoofed TCP segments. However, research has shown many concerns that the TCP MD5 algorithm is cryptographically ineffective with a ... CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2.2 BGP TCP Authentication Option (TCP-AO)

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. TCP-AO requires a shared secret profile with a valid lifetime and a per-neighbor configuration to use the shared secret. #show running-config section shared-secret management security session shared-secret profile TCPAO secret 1 7 $1c$G8BQN0ezkiJOX2cuAYpsEA== receive-lifetime 2026-01-01 00:00:00 2026-12-31 23:59:59 transmit-lifetime 2026-01-01 00:00:00 2026-12-31 23:59:59 router bgp 65013 neighbor {IP Address} password shared-secret profile TCPAO algorithm hmac-sha-256

remediation.command: Enable TCP-AO using the secret keys in Shared Secret Profile NAME with a specified algorithm: router bgp {ASN} neighbor NEIGHBOR_ID password shared-secret profile NAME algorithm ALGORITHM

title: Ensure the Management VRF Exists
description: Ensure that the mgmt vrf exists and is assigned to the interface that connects to the management network for out of band access. The switch has a dedicated management interface that should be assigned to this vrf. A Management VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) is a dedicated, isolated routing instance on a network device used exclusively for out-of-band management traffic. It separates administrator access (like SSH, SNMP, and Syslog) from production data traffic. CIS marks all EOS controls Manual; automated here: requires a 'vrf instance' and a Management interface placed in a VRF. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1.1 Ensure the Management VRF Exists

remediation.command: Creat a vrf, assign it to the management interface and create a static route to the rest of the network. The vrf instance should have a meaningful name and description indicating its purpose. vrf instance mgmt description Management VRF ! interface Management1 vrf mgmt ip route vrf mgmt 0/0 {Gateway Address} no ip routing vrf mgmt

title: Control Plane Policy Map
description: The default configuration comes with a pre-configured policy map to ensure adequate rate limiting for most traffic types punted to the CPU. Control plane policing can be used to increase the security of Arista switches by protecting the control plane from unnecessary or malicious traffic. It is recommended to implement control plane protection by classifying traffic types based on importance ... CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.3 Control Plane Policy Map

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Verify a policy map is applied to the control plane switch#show running-config all section system control-plane Expected output system control-plane ip access-group default-control-plane-acl in ip access-group default-control-plane-acl vrf MGMT in ipv6 access-group default-control-plane-acl in ipv6 access-group default-control-plane-acl vrf MGMT in service-policy input copp-system-policy switch# Check the configuration of the service policy #show policy-map type control-plane copp-system-policy Service-policy input: ...

remediation.command: If no policy is configured, enable the default policy system control-plane service-policy input copp-system-policy

title: Network Time Protocol
description: EOS enables Network Time Protocol (ntp) on the switch by default, and time settings from any properly configured ntp server override the manual setting of the system clock. ntp servers synchronize time settings of systems running an ntp client. The switch supports ntp versions 1 through 4, and uses version 4 by default. Without synchronized time accurately correlating information between devices becomes difficult, if not impossible. If logs cannot be successfully compared between each of the routers, switches, and firewalls, it will be very difficult to determine the exact ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.4 Network Time Protocol

title: DNS Configuration
description: It is recommended that a DNS server be defined for client resolver. This allows for the use of hostnames when configuring services such as ntp or syslog. The susceptibility of IP addresses to spoofing translates to DNS host name and IP address mapping vulnerabilities. For example, suppose a source host wishes to establish a connection with a destination host and queries a DNS server for the IP address of the ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.6 DNS Configuration

remediation.command:
! Configure at least one name server and a domain name. DNS services should be provided over the management network.
ip name-server {vrf [Management VRF]} {ip address}

title: Logging
description: Logging is a critical part of network security. Maintaining an audit trail of system activity logs (syslog) can help identify configuration errors, understand past intrusions, troubleshoot service disruptions, and react to probes and scans of the network. Syslog levels 0-6 are the levels required to collect the necessary information to help in the recovery process. It is recommended to log all messages except debugging and send all log data to a syslog server. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.7 Logging

title: VLAN Management
description: VLAN 1 is a special VLAN that tags and handles most of the control plane traffic. VLAN 1 is enabled on all trunks and ports by default. Ensure VLAN1 is pruned from all trunk and access ports that do not require it. Instability in one part of the network could affect VLAN 1, thereby influencing control-plane stability and therefore STP stability for all other VLANs. Checks that VLAN 1 is suspended; trunk allowed lists still need manual review. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.8 VLAN Management

remediation.command:
! vlan 1
state suspend
interface Ethernet[X]
switchport trunk allowed vlan except 1

title: Roles
description: A role consists of rules that permit or deny access to a set of commands within specified command modes. For local users a role limits the commands they can run to the appropriate set for their job. Additional custom roles can be defined as needed or AAA services - such as TACACS+ - can be used to provide more granular access to the switch. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3.1 Roles

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. show run all section ^role|username.*role This shows two local users with different roles username admin privilege 15 role network-admin secret sha512 XXXX username operations privilege 15 role network-operator secret sha512 XXX username user privilege 1 role network-admin nopassword role network-admin 10 permit command .* role network-operator 10 deny mode exec command configure|bash|python-shell|\| 20 permit mode exec command .*

remediation.command: Assign roles to local users with the username command username name [PRIVILEGE_LEVEL] SECURITY [ROLE_USER] SECURITY specifies the password assignment.

title: Idle Timeout
description: Tine out access to the console after a period of inactivity. Inactive unattended console sessions provide the opportunity for anyone with physical access to the device to make configuration changes enabling them to disrupt network operations resulting in a network outage. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.1 Idle Timeout

remediation.command:
! Configure idle timeout
configure
management console
idle-timeout ? <0-86400> Idle session timeout in minutes
idle-timeout 10

title: Emergency Console Access
description: Authentication for administrative access to the device should be required at all times. A single account should be created on the device's local database for use in an emergency such as when the authentication server is down or connectivity between the device and the authentication server is not operable. The console or emergency account logon credentials should be stored in a secure location. Console access should be available even if authentication servers are down or unreachable, but should not be accessible without authentication or with simple passwords. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.2 Emergency Console Access

remediation.command:
username admin privilege 15 role network-admin secret ? 0 Specify an UNENCRYPTED password will follow 5 Specify an ENCRYPTED MD5 password will follow LINE The UNENCRYPTED (cleartext) password sha512 Specifies an ENCRYPTED SHA512 password will follow * Specify a password that cannot be used to login
username admin privilege 15 role network-admin secret <password>

title: Server Groups
description: A server group is a collection of servers associated with a single group name. Subsequent authorization and authentication commands can access all servers in a group by invoking the group name. The switch supports TACACS+ and RADIUS server groups. Server groups allow AAA commands to access multiple servers, providing redundancy and load sharing. Before they are added to a group, servers must have been previously configured with a radius-server host or tacacs-server host command. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5.2 Server Groups

remediation.command: Configure a server group if required aaa group server tacacs+ TACPLUS server {ip address} server {ip address}

title: Remove cryptographically weak algorithms
description: Outdated and insecure ciphers and algorithms should not be used. An attacker can possibly break the encryption of transported data if weak ciphers and algorithms are used to access sensitive data. Fails if 'management ssh' does not restrict ciphers or lists a weak cipher, MAC or key-exchange method. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.6.3 Remove cryptographically weak algorithms

remediation.command: management ssh cipher aes128-ctr aes256-ctr key-exchange diffie-hellman-group14-sha256 mac hmac-sha2-256

title: Limit SNMP Access To Management VRF
description: SNMP access should be restricted to the management vrf. Detailed information about the network is sent across the network via SNMP. If this information is discovered by attackers it could be used to trace the network, show the network topology, and possibly gain access to network devices. Requires 'snmp-server vrf <mgmt>' and 'no snmp-server vrf default'. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.7.1 Limit SNMP Access To Management VRF

audit.pattern: (?m)(?s:^snmp-server vrf \S+.*^no snmp-server vrf default\s*$)|(?s:^no snmp-server vrf default\s*$.*^snmp-server vrf \S+)

remediation.command: snmp-server vrf {management VRF} no snmp-server vrf default

title: Use SNMPv3 Instead of Earlier Versions
description: The network element should use SNMP Version 3 for any SNMP agent configured on the device. SNMPv2 only requires a community string to be specified, which the client needs to use in their requests to "authenticate". SNMPv3 uses an actual security model called "User-based Security Model" (USM) codified in RFC3414 (originally in RFC2264 1998). Fails if no SNMPv3 group is defined or any group uses v1/v2c or lacks 'priv'. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.7.3 Use SNMPv3 Instead of Earlier Versions

remediation.command: snmp-server group group1 v3 priv snmp-server user user1 group1 v3 auth sha256 12345 priv aes256 {password} snmp-server host server1 version 3 priv user1

title: Login Banner
description: The login banner precedes the login prompt. Use a login banner to warn against unauthorized network access attempts or other messages to users. A legal banner is recommended on all external administrative interfaces. The purpose of a legal banner is to: - Provide Legal Protection should evidence need to be used from a device. - Act as a deterrent to potential intruders. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (not 'show running-config all').
reference: CIS Arista EOS Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.9.1 Login Banner

remediation.command:
! Configure a banner. An example banner is provided as a reference.
banner login Enter TEXT message. Type 'EOF' on its own line to end. * WARNING * This system is private and may be accessed only by authorized users for official purposes. The system owner reserves the right to monitor any and all activity taking place on this system and any attempts to connect to it. Individuals using this computer system are subject to having all of their activities monitored and recorded by system personnel. Use of this system evidences an express consent to such monitoring and agreement that if such monitoring reveals evidence of possible abuse or criminal activity, system personnel may provide the results of such monitoring to appropriate officials. Unauthorized users or users who exceed (or attempt to exceed), their authorized level of access are subject to prosecution under any local or international laws that apply as well as Company initiated proceedings. EOF
